headline: GH drains your T4
punch: This is why the standard panel misses it.

headline: Two ways a drug
body: So when people ask whether something affects your thyroid, they are almost always asking about production: does it change how much hormone your thyroid makes. That is the question TSH and T4 are designed to answer. | There is a second way, which is changing what happens to the hormone after it is made. GH works there, almost entirely, and that is precisely the mode of action that routine thyroid screening is worst at detecting.

headline: Where does your active T3 come from?
body: Your thyroid gland mostly outputs **T4**, which is close to biologically inert. The active hormone is **T3**, and the majority of it is manufactured outside the thyroid entirely, by enzymes called *deiodinases* that strip an iodine atom off T4 in peripheral tissue. | So your real thyroid status is largely a conversion question rather than an output question, and the two can move in opposite directions without anything being wrong with your gland.
punch: T4 is stock. T3 is the active form.

headline: GH speeds that up
body: GH upregulates **type 2 deiodinase**, the enzyme doing that conversion in peripheral tissue. The documented result following rhGH therapy is free T3 rising significantly, the free T3 to free T4 ratio rising, and reverse T3 falling. | And it is dose-dependent, with highly significant GH dose-dependent increases in total and free T3 as the dose rises. More growth hormone pulls more T4 across into T3.
punch: More GH means more T4 pulled into T3.

headline: Which sounds good
body: Here is the part that gets missed by everyone treating higher T3 as a straightforward win. Following GH replacement, **mean free T4 declined significantly**, by about 1.09 pmol/L. | The conversion did not manufacture T4 out of nothing. It consumed it. You are drawing from a reservoir faster than you were before, and the reservoir has a finite refill rate set by a gland that has no idea this is happening.
punch: ==T3 up. T4 down. Same hormone pool.==

headline: Now the trap
body: GH raises free T3 without changing T4 or TSH very much in the short term. So someone on growth hormone has **higher effective T3 activity than TSH and T4 alone would suggest**. | TSH is the number almost everyone screens with, and it is reporting on a pituitary feedback loop that this particular drug has partly stepped around. It is answering a question you are not actually asking.
punch: _TSH is answering a question you are not asking._

headline: And GH suppresses the signal too
body: On top of the conversion effect, GH suppresses TRH sensitivity at the hypothalamic level and blunts TSH pulsatility directly. At supraphysiological doses that central suppression is amplified further. | So the one number you would use to catch a developing problem is being pushed down by the same drug that is causing the problem. Two separate effects, both pointing in the direction of hiding it.
punch: Two effects. Both hide it from TSH.

headline: How often does it show up?
body: In adult hypopituitary patients, GH replacement has been reported to **unmask central hypothyroidism in 36 to 47%** of patients who appeared euthyroid beforehand, requiring thyroxine replacement afterwards. | Between a third and a half of a population that tested normal before starting. That is not a rare interaction buried in a case report, it is close to a coin flip in the population that was studied.

headline: Be precise about who
body: That figure comes from **hypopituitary adults**, people who already have established pituitary disease and are receiving GH as replacement for it. They are primed for exactly this to surface. | It is not a prediction about someone with an intact pituitary and normal thyroid reserve. What transfers to anyone else is the mechanism, which is general, not the percentage, which is specific to a sick population.
punch: A specific population. The mechanism is general.

headline: A bonus finding
body: The same paper notes that GH replacement also drives the conversion of **cortisol into cortisone**, its inactive form. So GH is inactivating a glucocorticoid at the same time it is activating a thyroid hormone. | Two separate endocrine axes, both shifted by GH in the direction of changing hormone activity rather than hormone quantity. Which is a pattern worth noticing, because it is invisible to any test that measures amount.
punch: GH moves conversion, not production, in both.

headline: What to take from this
body: GH shifts your thyroid system from storage toward activity, which raises T3 and drains T4, while simultaneously pushing down the marker you would use to catch it. | It is the same shape as everything else in this series. The headline number stays calm and the thing underneath it moves. A normal TSH on growth hormone is not evidence that nothing changed.
punch: ==A normal TSH is not evidence nothing changed.==
